comparator.name: Art History
comparator.sourceNotes: The live 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide public product identifies two 180-EC formal routes, Arts and Culture and Arts, Media and Society. The generic registry target is represented by the broad historical Arts and Culture route, independently of UCR fit. Its current structure totals 60 EC in each year: compulsory first-year visual analysis, art and architecture history, world art and academic skills; a 40-EC compulsory second year with 10 EC of two selected 5-EC seminars and a selected 10-EC Florence excursion; and a third year with 10 EC compulsory research/publishing, one 10-EC BA3 seminar, a 10-EC Art History final paper and genuine 30-EC open elective space. The first-listed early/modern seminar pair and Florence excursion provide one coherent instantiation of formal restricted choices. The public product API supplies the official module identities and EC; its curriculum grouping supplies compulsory and choice status. The 2025–26 archived study guide warned of 2026–27 changes, so it was not used to carry forward superseded course weights or choices.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum has eight art/archaeology/heritage courses, dedicated modern museum and art-historiography courses, visual media, source-based historical research and specific historical, literary and ethical complements. It follows the broad historic Arts and Culture route while acknowledging that UCR offers fewer art-specific courses and no equivalent thesis.

alternatives.concept: A contemporary visual-culture route that studies how art, film, exhibitions, digital media and communication shape social meaning, public debate and representation. It retains an art-historical base but gives substantially more weight to media and social theory than the historical Arts and Culture response.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme substantively covers all nine generator-eligible art-history, visual-object, architecture, heritage and historical-culture interests (rows 13552–13560). The remaining generator-eligible row 13561 and the current official Arts, Media and Society route support a coherent second programme with a distinct media/social-theory curriculum; its course sets differ by eight courses (60 EC) each way and both schedules satisfy the hard constraints. No further generator-eligible interest or independently evidenced third organising direction remains. Production therefore stops at two.

notes.text: Leiden’s Arts and Culture route gives sustained art-historical work across visual analysis, material techniques, architecture, several periods of European and world art, museums, heritage, aesthetics, specialised seminars and an Art History final paper. UCR offers a smaller art-history and heritage sequence and adds relevant history, archaeology, media and cultural-analysis courses; it does not reproduce the full specialist sequence or dedicated final paper.
